verdict.rationale: Sentry's own docs say code mappings link stack trace paths to source paths in your repository. They state this enables suspect commits, stack trace linking and code owners, which covers the core of the story; Suspect Commits, Associate Commits and Ownership Rules pages back this up, though only as titles. missing for 10: documented repo-integration setup (e.g., GitHub connection), explicit evidence that stack-frame links resolve to the exact line on the default branch, detail beyond feature titles for suspect commits and ownership, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the platform connects to my repos so an issue shows suspect commits and code owners, and I can jump from a stack frame to the exact line on my default branch

citations.quote: Code mappings link stack trace paths to source code paths in your repository. They enable features like source context, suspect commits, stack trace linking, and code owners.
Code mappings link stack trace paths to source code paths in your repository, enabling source context, suspect commits, and code owners.
